messages.content:
You are identifying variation axes for AI risk concepts using ontology classes.

A variation axis is an ontology class that represents a dimension along which diverse prompts can be generated. Each axis has a semantic role relative to the risk:
- agent: Who performs or is affected by the action
- object: What is acted upon
- instrument: What tool/means is used
- location: Where it occurs
- temporal: When it occurs

Given a risk (with description and concern) and candidate ontology classes (with definitions and siblings), select the classes that are most semantically relevant to the risk.

Return 2-3 axes max.

Risk: Offensive cyber capabilities
Description: Lowered barriers for offensive cyber capabilities, including via automated discovery and exploitation of vulnerabilities to ease hacking, malware, phishing, offensive cyber operations, or other cyberattacks; increased attack surface for targeted cyberattacks, which may compromise a system’s availability or the confidentiality or integrity of training data, code, or model weights.
Concern: None
Policy: Insider Threat & Cybersecurity

Candidate ontology classes:
- https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontology/SEC/Securities/SecuritiesIdentification/SecurityIdentifier: security identifier — any publicly available identifier that is used to identify a security [found by 21/67 queries]
  Siblings: unique product identifier, unique swap identifier, universal loan identifier
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/RegulatoryAgencies/RegulatoryReport: regulatory report — document required to support operational transparency that demonstrates compliance with some specification, law, policy, restriction, or other rule specified by a regulatory agency [found by 46/67 queries]
  Siblings: technical specification document, registry, transaction record
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/PartiesAndSituations/SoftwareAgent: software agent — digital entity that perceives its environment and takes actions that maximize its chance of successfully achieving its goals [found by 41/67 queries]
  Siblings: automated underwriting system, automated system, party
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/Documents/TechnicalSpecificationDocument: technical specification document — document that sets out detailed requirements to be satisfied by a product, material, process or system and the procedures for checking conformity to these requirements [found by 39/67 queries]
  Siblings: regulatory report, formula, observable value
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#HarmfulHowTo: Harmful How-To — Step-by-step instructions for activities that cause property destruction, physical harm, or enable illegal intrusion when executed by unauthorized individuals. [found by 36/67 queries]
  Siblings: CBRN Information, Drug Synthesis, Dual-Use Research Concern
- https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontology/SEC/Securities/SecuritiesIdentification/SecurityIdentificationScheme: security identification scheme — formal definition of the structure and application of a particular set of securities identifiers [from restriction: isDefinedIn on SecurityIdentifier]
- https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontology/FBC/FinancialInstruments/FinancialInstruments/Security: security — financial instrument that can be bought or sold [from restriction: identifies on SecurityIdentifier]
  Siblings: spot contract, debt instrument, over-the-counter instrument

axes.rationale: The risk describes 'lowered barriers for offensive cyber capabilities, including via automated discovery and exploitation of vulnerabilities... or other cyberattacks.' The Harmful How-To class directly captures step-by-step instructions for illegal intrusion, which is the core mechanism of the described threat.

The risk mentions 'automated discovery and exploitation of vulnerabilities' and 'malware, phishing, offensive cyber operations.' A software agent is a digital entity that takes actions to achieve goals, making it semantically relevant for the actors (or automated components) performing the attacks.

The risk concerns compromising 'training data, code, or model weights' and the general nature of cyberattacks often involves exploiting weaknesses detailed in technical specifications. This class represents the type of information or requirement that could be targeted or used to define the attack surface.
